flexion.label: Flexural Crack
flexion.short_description: Vertical crack caused by bending stress, typically at midspan of beams or slabs.
common_causes: Tensile stress at the bottom fiber of beams under gravity loads
Insufficient longitudinal reinforcement or inadequate reinforcement detailing
Service loads exceeding the cracking moment of the section
Loss of prestress in prestressed members
visual_indicators: Vertical orientation, perpendicular to the element axis
Located near midspan on the tension face (bottom of simply-supported beams, top of cantilevers)
Uniform spacing between multiple parallel cracks
Crack width typically narrows towards the neutral axis

severity_thresholds.minor: Width below 0.3 mm, limited depth, no corrosion signs
severity_thresholds.moderate: Width 0.3–0.5 mm, visible propagation but stable
severity_thresholds.severe: Width above 0.5 mm, rebar exposure, or active propagation

recommended_actions: Measure crack width with crack comparator
Document location relative to support and midspan
If width exceeds 0.4 mm, schedule structural evaluation
Monitor propagation over 30–90 days with date-stamped photos

asentamiento.label: Settlement Crack
asentamiento.short_description: Diagonal stair-step crack caused by differential foundation settlement.
common_causes: Non-uniform soil bearing capacity under foundations
Expansive or collapsible soils
Water infiltration or leakage eroding subgrade
Adjacent construction disturbing existing foundations
Overloaded foundation beyond design capacity
visual_indicators: Diagonal stair-step pattern following mortar joints in masonry
Diagonal orientation in monolithic walls, typically propagating from openings
Progressively wider from one end to the other
Often extends through multiple elements (wall, slab, beam)
May be accompanied by door/window misalignment

severity_thresholds.minor: Width below 1 mm, stable over time, single wall affected
severity_thresholds.moderate: Width 1–3 mm, visible in multiple elements, may affect serviceability
severity_thresholds.severe: Width above 3 mm, active propagation, structural distress evident

recommended_actions: Install crack monitors (Avongard or similar) to track movement over time
Investigate foundation condition and soil behavior
Check for water leaks near the foundation
Geotechnical assessment required for moderate/severe cases
Do not perform cosmetic repair before resolving the underlying cause

cortante.label: Shear Crack
cortante.short_description: Diagonal crack at approximately 45° caused by shear stress, typically near supports.
common_causes: Insufficient shear reinforcement (stirrups) or excessive spacing
Concentrated loads near supports
Seismic loading inducing diagonal tension
Loss of bond between concrete and shear reinforcement
visual_indicators: Diagonal orientation at approximately 45° to the element axis
Located near supports of beams or at column ends
May propagate from bottom tension zone upward
Multiple parallel diagonal cracks indicate critical shear condition
Often widens rapidly if not addressed

severity_thresholds.minor: Single hairline diagonal crack, width below 0.3 mm
severity_thresholds.moderate: Width 0.3–0.6 mm, stable, limited to one location
severity_thresholds.severe: Width above 0.6 mm, multiple parallel cracks, or active propagation — potential imminent failure

recommended_actions: Immediate structural assessment — shear failure is typically brittle and sudden
Do not apply additional loading to the element
Evacuate area under severe cracks until assessed
Consider temporary shoring if near supports of critical elements
Document with photos including scale reference

corrosion.label: Corrosion-Induced Crack
corrosion.short_description: Longitudinal crack along reinforcement caused by rebar corrosion and expansion.
common_causes: Chloride ingress from marine environments or deicing salts
Carbonation of concrete cover reducing alkalinity
Insufficient concrete cover over reinforcement
Cracks or porosity allowing moisture and oxygen access to rebar
Stray electrical currents
visual_indicators: Longitudinal crack parallel to reinforcement direction
Rust staining along the crack line
Concrete cover spalling or delamination
Exposed corroded reinforcement in advanced cases
Surface efflorescence adjacent to crack

severity_thresholds.minor: Surface staining only, no delamination, minimal cover loss
severity_thresholds.moderate: Visible delamination, partial cover loss, cross-section reduction below 10%
severity_thresholds.severe: Exposed rebar, cross-section loss above 10%, loss of bond with concrete

recommended_actions: Perform chloride content and carbonation depth tests
Use half-cell potential testing to map corrosion activity
Remove deteriorated concrete to sound substrate
Clean and treat reinforcement before patching
Apply corrosion inhibitor or cathodic protection for severe cases
Address environmental exposure source (sealants, coatings)

acabados.label: Finishing / Surface Crack
acabados.short_description: Shallow surface crack limited to plaster, render, or finishing coat without structural significance.
common_causes: Differential shrinkage between substrate and finishing layer
Inadequate curing of plaster or render
Thermal movement of the finishing layer
Poor adhesion to substrate
Application over insufficiently cured concrete
visual_indicators: Very narrow width, typically below 0.2 mm
Limited depth, does not penetrate the structural substrate
Often follows a fine random pattern
May appear only in the finishing layer, not continuous with structural concrete
No associated structural deformation

severity_thresholds.minor: Hairline cracks in finishing only, aesthetic concern
severity_thresholds.moderate: Visible pattern, localized debonding of finish from substrate
severity_thresholds.severe: Finish detachment, water infiltration risk to structural substrate

recommended_actions: Verify crack is limited to finishing layer (tap test for hollow sounds)
For aesthetic repair: clean, apply flexible sealant or repaint
For water-exposed surfaces: apply waterproof coating after repair
If cracks reappear after repair, investigate substrate conditions
Not a structural concern unless associated with substrate cracking

retraccion.label: Shrinkage Crack
retraccion.short_description: Crack caused by concrete volumetric contraction during drying or curing.
common_causes: Drying shrinkage in hardened concrete
Plastic shrinkage during setting (surface evaporation)
High water-cement ratio in the mix
Inadequate curing (insufficient moisture retention)
Restrained shrinkage due to fixed edges or embedded elements
Large unjointed slab areas
visual_indicators: Random orientation, often map-like pattern on slabs
Relatively uniform width throughout the crack length
Typically shallow, rarely full-depth in slabs
Appears within days to weeks of placement (plastic) or months (drying)
No structural distress or deformation associated

severity_thresholds.minor: Width below 0.3 mm, stable, no water passage
severity_thresholds.moderate: Width 0.3–0.5 mm, may allow water infiltration
severity_thresholds.severe: Width above 0.5 mm, full-depth in slabs, durability concern

recommended_actions: Monitor for stability — drying shrinkage cracks typically stabilize after 1–2 years
For water-tight requirements: seal with flexible polyurethane sealant
For slabs exposed to vehicular traffic: epoxy injection to restore load transfer
Not a structural concern in most cases
Review curing practices for future placements

cuarteado.label: Crazing / Map Cracking
cuarteado.short_description: Fine network of shallow surface cracks forming polygonal pattern.
common_causes: Carbonation shrinkage of the cement paste at the surface
Premature finishing operations trapping bleed water
Overworking of the finished surface
Rapid drying of the surface after placement
Alkali-silica reaction in advanced cases
Freeze-thaw damage in cold climates
visual_indicators: Network of fine interconnected cracks forming polygonal cells
Individual cells typically 25–75 mm across
Cracks very shallow, often limited to surface paste
Visible primarily when surface is wet or under oblique light
May be accompanied by surface dusting or scaling

severity_thresholds.minor: Surface pattern visible only when wet, no material loss
severity_thresholds.moderate: Visible when dry, minor surface scaling
severity_thresholds.severe: Deep pattern with spalling, underlying ASR or freeze-thaw confirmed

recommended_actions: Typically aesthetic concern only — assess depth before repair
If due to ASR: perform petrographic examination and monitor expansion
Apply penetrating sealer to reduce moisture ingress
For exposed surfaces: consider topping slab or overlay
Prevent in new work with proper curing and finishing practices

disclaimer: This tool provides preliminary classification and general guidance based on ACI standards. It does not replace professional structural evaluation. Always consult a licensed structural engineer for definitive assessment and repair decisions.
